# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 🙏]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👆 ✊]

I see the bomb: display reads 0, light is yellow, and there are three wires — 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. I hear nothing, so all I have is what I see plus the gestures that just arrived.

The gestures are for me (Deaf), from Mute and Blind. But I need to be careful: I can see gestures, and I can speak to Mute and Blind. Blind cannot see gestures, only feel the bomb. Mute can read the manual and can hear my speech.

Mute gestured [👆 🙏] — index finger, folded hands/pray. Blind gestured [✋ 👆 ✊] — flat hand, index finger, fist.

I don't yet know what these mean. They may be referencing wire positions or actions. I should describe my view plainly so Mute (who has the manual) can match it to a rule, and so Blind (who can touch) knows what I see. I'll speak to both, and gesture back to Mute since Mute can see gestures.

I'll describe: display 0, yellow light, wires yellow/green/blue in positions 1/2/3. I'll also gesture an acknowledgment and ask for meaning — but gestures carry no words, so I'll keep them simple: maybe point to wire 1 and 2 and 3? Actually I should just send my visual facts via speech, which reaches both Mute and Blind. Blind needs the colors and positions since they can't see them.

Let me speak to everyone (unnamed reaches Mute and Blind). Then gesture to Mute only, since Blind can't see gestures.

```
speak(text="I see the bomb. Display shows 0. Light is yellow. Three wires in positions: 1 is yellow, 2 is green, 3 is blue.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👆", "✋", "✊"])
```

Wait — I should not just echo their gestures back blindly; that could be misread. But I have no shared code yet. Better to gesture something that anchors: point at wire 1, wire 2, wire 3 in order, so Mute can associate my gestures with positions. Actually gestures are just symbols, not pointing at real objects. The symbols themselves are the alphabet. So [👆 ✌ ✊] could mean "1, 2, 3"? Not established.

I'll keep it minimal: acknowledge and give my view in speech. Gesture a simple "received" — maybe 🙏 back to Mute. But that risks confusion.

Let me just speak the facts and gesture the wire order as numbers if I can: 👆=1, ✌=2, ✊=3 is a plausible convention but not agreed. I'll propose it.

Actually, safest: speak everything, and gesture a clear proposal to Mute: [👆 ✌ ✊] meaning positions 1,2,3. Mute can then use the manual.

I'll finalize.

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌 ✋]

I see the bomb now: display 0, light has changed to **red**, wires unchanged — 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue.

New gestures arrived: Mute sent [✌ ✊] (two, fist) and Blind sent [👌 ✋] (OK, flat hand). Still no agreed code, but I notice Mute's previous [👆 🙏] and now [✌ ✊] — the first symbol incremented from 👆(1) to ✌(2). That looks like Mute is counting or indexing something. Blind's [✋ 👆 ✊] then [👌 ✋] — less clear.

The light changed from yellow to red between turns. That's a real change I must report. Display still 0.

I can't hear, so I don't know if Mute or Blind are speaking to me — I only get gestures. I should keep broadcasting my visual facts so Mute (manual) and Blind (hands) can act. I'll speak to both, and gesture to Mute to try to establish wire-position code: I'll gesture [👆 ✌ ✊] to anchor positions 1,2,3, then gesture the colors? Colors have no gesture names. So I can only give positions numerically.

Let me speak the change clearly and gesture the position numbers.

```
speak(text="Update: light is now RED, was yellow last round. Display still 0. Wires: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👆", "✌", "✊"])
```

That anchors positions. Mute can map colors via my speech.
